title: Tenant snapshot schemas and certified evidence bundles for request artifacts
creator: Avery Lin
description:
Problem: Customers in regulated industries require tamper-evident, auditable exports of request artifacts (prompts, responses, request logs, and derived metrics) scoped to tenant residency and tenant-specific retention policies. Existing exports are ad-hoc JSON dumps without strong provenance metadata, making audits and cross-region compliance difficult.

This ticket: Define a tenant-level snapshot schema (v1) and implement a certified evidence bundle export flow that packages request artifacts with immutable manifests, cryptographic hashes, residency markers, retention metadata, and automated attestations. The export must support auditor-friendly formats, region-aware encryption, KMS-backed signing of manifests, and a verification CLI to validate bundle integrity and retention status. The feature should be available via Console (Export UI), API, and a scheduled snapshot job for Compliance Plan customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Schema v1 published in Confluence and used by export job.
2) Evidence bundle output format: signed TAR.GZ containing artifacts directory (JSONL for prompts/responses, Parquet for metrics), manifest.json (SHA256 checksums, object paths, residency tags, retention TTLs, schema_version), and attestation.sig (KMS-signed).
3) Export supports tenant-scoped residency labeling and enforces region-only exports if tenant residency is 'EU-only' or 'US-only'.
4) Console UI has an Export button and a scheduling option with timezone-aware start, retention preview, and destination S3/GCS config.
5) API endpoint /v1/exports accepts filter by time window, routes to correct region, returns job id and signed download URL on completion.
6) CLI verify-bundle validates checksums and signature using public key and produces human-readable audit report.
7) End-to-end test coverage for export job, encryption/signing, and CLI verification.
8) Security review completed and signed off by Security.
9) Documentation and runbook for auditors and support engineers published.
implementation_notes:
- Schema v1 fields: bundle_id, tenant_id, created_at, time_window.start, time_window.end, residency_tag, retention_policy_id, artifacts: {prompts.jsonl, responses.jsonl, logs.jsonl, metrics.parquet}, manifest entries with SHA256 and byte_size.
- Use KMS asymmetric key to sign manifest.json; store public key in Control Plane and publish for auditors.
- Export worker will stream artifacts to staging S3 bucket in tenant-region, compute incremental checksums to avoid memory spikes.
- Support output compression with reproducible tar ordering to make signatures deterministic.
- Retention enforcement: if tenant retention < export TTL, the manifest must include retention_override flag and export blocked unless flagged as 'for-audit' with explicit approver.
- RBAC: only org-admins and compliance-role can trigger tenant-level exports. API uses machine-token scopes: exports:write and exports:read.
- Telemetry: expose token-level export counts, average bundle size, time-to-complete, and failures; hook into Console Dashboard.
- Provide optional 'evidence-certification' webhook that posts signed manifest metadata to customer audit endpoint on completion.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal beta): enable for 10 sandbox tenants; feature flag off for public. Verify signing and CLI validation.
Phase 2 (pilot customers): enable for 3 compliance customers with dedicated support. Collect feedback and measure export times and bundle sizes.
Phase 3 (general availability): enable Console and API exports for all tenants on Compliance Plan; publish docs and support runbook.
Fallback: if signing KMS unavailable, fallback to unsigned manifest but mark bundle as 'unsigned' and require manual approval for release.
risks: Large tenants may produce multi-GB bundles and hit memory/timeout limits on workers
Cross-region encryption keys complexity may delay exports for EU-residency tenants
Edge case: in-flight deletions conflicting with retention policy snapshots could produce inconsistent manifests
qa_plan:
Create synthetic dataset generator that builds 3 tenant profiles (small/medium/large) and runs full export cycles. Verify file formats, checksums, signature validation. Run integration tests for region restrictions (set tenant.residency to EU-only and assert export fails for US bucket targets). Add negative tests for retention override enforcement.
Manual QA: security to validate KMS signing and public key distribution; compliance to review bundle contents for audit readiness.
comments: 2026-02-16: Initial scoping review with Eng and Security. Decided to use KMS asymmetric signing vs HMAC to allow third-party verification.
2026-02-20: Design review — UX requested an inline retention-preview modal showing estimated preserved object counts and byte size before scheduling export (Marco to prototype).
2026-02-28: Engineering spike (ENG-2104) completed: streaming checksum writer implemented; memory footprint reduced by 70% in prototype. See GH PR linked below.
2026-03-04: Security review opened. Principal Security Engineer flagged need for key rotation policy and attestation chain. Security requested a runbook for key compromise scenarios.
2026-03-09: UX mock updated. Prototype includes 'Force export for audit' checkbox that requires two approvers for retention-override. PM to validate legal requirements for two-approver flows.
2026-03-12: Blocker: cross-region KMS permissions cause export failures in EU test tenant. Eng has follow-up task ENG-2248 to add region-aware IAM roles. Keeping ticket In Progress.
notes: This ticket intentionally targets a certified bundle format to reduce ad-hoc audit requests and decrease SRE time spent assembling evidence. We expect a measurable drop in support time for audit requests after pilot (hypothesis: 60% reduction).
